observations: body L1-L11: the end of the sentence begun on p. 322. The numbers are right, with the signs counted from Sunday as 1: thirty Arab years have 10631 days, 1518 weeks and 5 days; 210 years have 74417 days, exactly 10631 weeks; the astronomical epoch of the hijrah, 15 July 622, was a Thursday (5), and a common year 0 of 354 days before it, 50 weeks and 4 days, gives the sign 1. The table of vol. II, p. 7 agrees: the collected years 30, 60, ..., 210 have the signs 5, 3, 1, 6, 4, 2, 7 (5 for each thirty years, counted from the sign 0), the single years 1 to 30 the signs 5, 2, 7, ..., 6 that follow from the year 1 with the leap years 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26 and 29; so the year 30 has the sign 6 among the single years and 5 among the collected ones, as L10-L11 say. The signs of multiplication are set as $\times$. The hyphens of «descri-», «anno-» and «nume-» measure 2.3, 2.0 and 2.5 pt.

body L12-L17: «al–Battānī» (L12) and «Albatenium» are letter-spaced, «al–Battānī» (L15) not; the dashes measure 5.2 and 5.3 pt. «al–Khāzinī» is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.2 pt). The rule of L14-L15 is p. 145, L16-L17 of the translation.

body L18-L28: the dash after «II.» measures 9.8 pt. The ellipses are set as printed: five dots before «VIII», «XIX», «XXVII», «VII», «XXVI», «27», «18» and «26», four before «XVIII» and «19», the last dot a little apart. The leap years of the table of vol. II, p. 7 as printed are 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26 and 29, those that Nallino restores. «Ḥabash» (L26), «al–Bīrūnī» and «Sachau» are letter-spaced, «Ḥabash» (L24, L27) not; «9–18», «197–98» and «178–80» have long dashes (5.4, 5.3 and about 5 pt, the last joined to the 8), as has «al–Bīrūnī» (5.3 pt).

body L29-L36: the head is set in capitals and small capitals; the dash after «a)» measures 9.7 pt, that of «145–146» 5.3 pt. The place is pp. 145-146 of the translation, appendix B. «al–Battānī» (L31) is letter-spaced; the dashes of «’l–qarnayn» and «al–Battānī» measure 5.3 and 5.0 pt. The note cited is a) on chapter XXXII, p. 242, where the epoch of the era is given as Saturday, 1 September 312. The Julian years return to their order of weekdays after 28 years, 10227 days or 1461 weeks, as L33-L34 say. The o of «post» (L33) prints in part. The hyphen of «uni-» measures 2.4 pt.
body L37-L43: «Albatenii» (L37) is letter-spaced. The argument is right: a common Julian year of 365 days moves the signs by one, a leap year of 366 days by two. The hyphen of «ve-» measures 1.9 pt.
